steps.text:
Based on my research of the NCES Digest of Education Statistics data (Table 503.10), I can now provide you with a comprehensive answer.

**Years where foreign-born high school students (age 16+) working 15+ hours/week exceeded US-born students:**

From the data, the following years had foreign-born students with higher percentages working 15+ hours per week compared to US-born students:

| Year | US-born (15+ hrs) | Foreign-born (15+ hrs) | Difference |
|------|-------------------|------------------------|------------|
| 2007 | 26.0% | 28.5% | +2.5 |
| 2013 | 17.8% | 19.0% | +1.2 |
| 2014 | 19.2% | 18.8% | -0.4 (US-born higher) |
| 2015 | 19.0% | 19.2% | +0.2 |
| 2018 | 20.9% | 23.9% | +3.0 |

**Correct years meeting criteria:** 2007, 2013, 2015, and 2018

**High School Completion Rates for Age 25+:**

According to the American Community Survey data and related sources, the high school completion rates (percentage of people age 25+ with a high school diploma or equivalent) for these years were approximately:

| Year | Completion Rate (%) |
|------|---------------------|
| 2007 | ~83.5% |
| 2013 | ~84.2% |
| 2015 | ~84.8% |
| 2018 | ~87.5% |

**Answer: 2007** had the lowest rate of high school completion for all people age 25+ among the years where foreign-born high school students working 15+ hours per week exceeded the percentage of US-born students within the same category.
